sights.w: The 374-step stairway (1881) cut straight up the hillside from Hors-Château to the Citadelle, built so soldiers could reach town without the alleys — Liège's emblem and its best free climb, with a panorama over the roofs and the Meuse.
Santiago Calatrava's white steel-and-glass vault (2009) — a station with no façade, just a 160 m canopy over the tracks; worth the detour even if you arrive by car.

sights.address: Parc de la Boverie 3, 4020 Liège, Belgium
sights.w: The city's fine-arts museum in a 1905 Exhibition palace on the Boverie island park, with a glass extension for blockbuster shows run in partnership with the Louvre; Ingres, Monet, Picasso and the Walloon school.

sights.address: Place de la Cathédrale, 4000 Liège, Belgium
sights.w: Gothic cathedral since 1802 (after the revolutionaries razed Saint-Lambert); its Trésor holds the reliquary bust of Saint Lambert and the gold reliquary Charles the Bold gave in penance for sacking the city.

The 1930s Sauvenière swimming baths, an Art Deco modernist landmark, reborn as a civic culture centre with exhibitions on memory and citizenship (incl. the permanent 'Plus jamais ça!' Holocaust route).
The Province's folk-life museum in the 17th-c. Friars Minor convent — a century of Walloon everyday life, crafts, dialect and the Liège puppets (with marionnette shows).

One of the four UNESCO 'Major Mining Sites of Wallonia' and one of only a handful of European coal mines you can still descend — ex-miners guide you 30 and 60 m down the shafts of the Trembleur colliery (closed 1980).
Cistercian abbey founded 1216 in the green Berwinne valley of the Herve plateau, on the Council of Europe's Cistercian route — and the home of Val-Dieu abbey beer, brewed on site.
The Dutch-built (1818–23) citadel crowning the rock above the Meuse at Huy — a Nazi prison and Gestapo jail in WWII, now a memorial museum with sweeping river views.
Gothic collegiate church on the Meuse with the great rose window 'Li Rondia' and a treasury holding Mosan reliquary shrines of the 12th–13th c.

Victor Besme's 1880 octagonal pavilion over Spa's most famous iron-rich spring, named for Peter the Great who took the cure here in 1717 — taste the water, see the Livre d'Or painting of famous curistes.
The 7 km Ardennes circuit of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1921 and its legendary Eau Rouge–Raidillon climb; tours, a museum in Stavelot abbey and race weekends all season.

Under Place Saint-Lambert: the excavated foundations of the vanished Cathedral of Saint-Lambert (razed 1794), a Gallo-Roman villa and finds back to the Mesolithic — the city's birthplace, walked underground.
Former Benedictine abbey church with a flamboyant-Gothic nave under a dazzling painted star vault, a Romanesque westwork and a Renaissance portal — Liège's most beautiful interior.
Museum of the 'Free Republic of Outremeuse' devoted to Tchantchès, Liège's cheeky wooden-puppet hero — his costumes, the Bisscheroux marionettes and puppet shows in season.
The 1820 neoclassical Théâtre royal, Wallonia's opera house, with a modern rooftop extension; Grétry's heart is in an urn at the foot of his statue outside.

sights.address: Quai Édouard Van Beneden 22, 4020 Liège, Belgium
sights.w: The University of Liège's aquarium (2,500 fish in some 50 tanks) and zoological museum in the 19th-c. Institut de Zoologie on the Meuse — a whale skeleton, dioramas and a cabinet of curiosities.
One of Liège's seven collegiate churches (founded c. 987) with a fortress-like Romanesque tower; inside, a carved Brabant altarpiece of the Passion of St Denis (early 16th c.).

sights.address: Coteaux de la Citadelle, 4000 Liège, Belgium
sights.w: 86 ha of terraced hillside orchards, vineyards, stairways and alleys between Hors-Château and the Citadelle — Liège's green lung, laureate of the Council of Europe Landscape Award; walk the Terrasses des Minimes for the views.
The old market square in front of the 18th-c. town hall 'La Violette', ringed by café terraces; the Perron fountain at its centre is the symbol of Liège's civic liberties since the Middle Ages.
An 18th-c. merchant-banker's mansion on Féronstrée kept as a period house museum — Liège furniture, Cordoba leather wall-hangings, tapestries and stucco ceilings of the prince-bishops' golden age.

sights.n: Maison de la Métallurgie et de l'Industrie de Liège
sights.w: Industrial-heritage museum in the old Espérance-Longdoz steelworks — a working 17th-c.-style forge, blast-furnace models and the story of the coal and steel that made Liège.

sights.n: Musée des Transports en commun de Wallonie
sights.w: Old Vennes tram depot full of Liège trams, trolleybuses and buses from horse-drawn days on — a nostalgic stop now the city's new tram is running again.

The Interallied Memorial on the Cointe hill: a 75 m tower and a basilica raised in the 1930s by the WWI Allies to honour the 1914 defence of Liège — the lift up the tower gives the city's best panorama.

sights.n: Musée en plein air du Sart-Tilman
sights.w: A free open-air museum of 120+ contemporary sculptures and murals by Belgian and international artists spread across the University of Liège's wooded Sart-Tilman campus.
Show cave on the Amblève at Aywaille, visited since 1828 — a walk through the Cathedral chamber ending in what is billed as the longest underground boat ride in the world (≈600 m on the Rubicon).
Belgium's best-known waterfall, a 15 m double cascade of the Amblève created by monks cutting a meander in the 18th c.; a chairlift climbs to the Montagne de Lancre viewpoint above.

Ruined 11th–16th-c. fortress on a rock above Theux, seat of the marquisate of Franchimont — remembered for the 600 Franchimontois who tried to kill Charles the Bold in 1468; climbable casemates and towers.
Belgium's highest point (694 m) on the Hautes Fagnes plateau — the gateway to the raised-bog boardwalks of the High Fens nature reserve.
The former Cistercian abbey on the Meuse at Seraing where Val-Saint-Lambert has blown lead crystal since 1826 — the Cristal Discovery visit shows glassblowers at work and two centuries of pieces.

sights.address: Quai de la Batte, 4000 Liège, Belgium
sights.w: Every Sunday morning since 1561: Belgium's oldest and biggest street market stretches 2 km along the Meuse quays — fruit, Herve cheese, live poultry, flowers, books, and péket and gaufres to keep you going.

sights.address: Colline d'Annette et Lubin, Spa, Belgium
sights.w: The modern glass thermal baths on Annette-et-Lubin hill, reached by funicular from the town centre — naturally carbonated Spa waters in the town that gave every 'spa' its name, a UNESCO Great Spa Town of Europe since 2021.

sights.n: Musée de la Ville d'eaux (Villa Royale)
sights.w: In Queen Marie-Henriette's Villa Royale: the story of Spa as Europe's 'Café of Europe' resort, with the painted-wood 'Jolités de Spa' souvenirs; the Spa horse museum is in the stables.

The former prince-abbey of Stavelot-Malmedy, its 11th-c. church foundations laid open, now three museums: the Principality's history, Guillaume Apollinaire, and the Spa-Francorchamps circuit museum of F1 cars and bikes.
